\begin{lemma}[Boolean encoding of a proposition]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.ite_bool}
\label{Complexity.Codec.ite_bool}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For any type $\alpha$, proposition $p$ with a decision procedure, and function
$f:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\alpha$, the value that is $f(\mathrm{true})$ when
$p$ holds and $f(\mathrm{false})$ otherwise is $f(\mathrm{decide}(p))$, where
$\mathrm{decide}(p)$ is true exactly when $p$ holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation of a head movement]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pm_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pm_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.cast, Complexity.Codec.Reach.single', Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val_Pos, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val_Pos2, Complexity.Codec.SInfo, Complexity.Codec.aI, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.gd_of, Complexity.Codec.ite_bool, Complexity.Codec.movePos, Complexity.Codec.pmNext, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $y$
be a finite Boolean word, and let $I$ be a simulated state together with the recorded
head and tape information. For Boolean flags $b,f$, define the register bound
$B=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, and let $R$ be a register file in which every register is at most
$B$, with $1\le R.N1$, $R.Pos\le R.N1$, and $R.N1+1\le B$. In step mode, the program
reaches its next phase with register file unchanged; that phase is selected according as
moving the input head from position $R.Pos$, with boundary parameter $R.N1-1$ and
movement prescribed by $I$ and $b$, yields position $R.Pos2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability after encoding the input symbol]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.z_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.z_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.single', Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.VSt, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.gd_of, Complexity.Codec.inpOf, Complexity.Codec.zcode, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and work-tape
symbols. Let $y,x$ be finite bit strings, let $\sigma$ be a verifier state, let $R$ be a
register assignment whose 21 values are all at most $B=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, and let $p$ be
a natural number. Write $\iota(x,p)$ for the input symbol at position $p$, taking the
value “blank” when $p$ is either boundary position and otherwise the bit of $x$ at index
$p-1$ (defaulting to $0$ if that index is beyond $x$). Encode these three possibilities
by $0$ for blank, $1$ for false, and $2$ for true. If register $Z$ equals this code,
then for some $z\le 2$ the codec program in step mode can reach the phase that starts
processing the symbol $\iota(x,p)$, changing only register $Z$ to $z$ and keeping every
register at most $B$ throughout the run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance and transition answer]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.stepAns}
\label{Complexity.Codec.stepAns}

Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a
finite Boolean input, and let $st$ be a verifier state, with positions
$p,p'\in\mathbb{N}$ and Boolean lists $u,u'$. The function returns true exactly when
$st$ is accepting and at least one of the two transition choices (false or true) moves
the input head from position $p$ to $p'$ and satisfies the corresponding completion
condition, using the scan result on $u,u'$ for that choice.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and $k$ work tapes, and
let $y,x,w,w',r$ be Boolean lists such that $y$ is obtained by successively
pair-encoding $x$, $w$, and the pair-encoding of $w'$ with $r$. Let $s$ be a natural
number, $st$ a virtual configuration accumulator, and $R$ a register assignment. Suppose
every register of $R$ is at most $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W$ is the chunk width
determined by $N$; also suppose $R_{N1}=|x|+1$, $R_{Pos}\le |x|+1$, $R_Z$ is the code of
the input symbol at position $R_{Pos}$, $R_{Q3}=2|x|+2$, $R_{Q4}=2|x|+2|w|+4$, and
$R_E=2|x|+2+4Ws+2W$. If $W(2s+1)\le |w|$, $W(2s+1)\le |w'|$, and $s\le 2|y|$, then the
step-mode register program, using its specified oracle, halts from the configuration
with accumulator $st$ and register assignment $R$, keeps all registers within the stated
bound, and returns the step predicate evaluated at $x$, $st$, positions $R_{Pos}$ and
$R_{Pos2}$, and the prefixes of $w$ and $w'$ of length $W(2s+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Boolean Step Test Characterization]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.stepAns_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.stepAns_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.PreChk, Complexity.Codec.StepChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.stepAns, Complexity.Codec.vScan, Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,w,w'$
be Boolean lists, and let $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $w$ has the prescribed
configuration-code length, its designated terminal bit is true, and the integer encoded
in its input-position field is at most $|x|+1$. Assume also that $w'$ has the prescribed
code length and its designated terminal bit is true. Then the Boolean step test on the
configuration portion and input-position fields of $w,w'$ equals true if and only if the
step-check predicate holds: $w$ is a valid configuration code, $w'$ has the required
length and terminal bit, and some nondeterministic choice gives the prescribed
input-head position update and passes the local tape-update check between the
configuration portions of $w$ and $w'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Shape of a two-payload code]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.shape2_of_code}
\label{Complexity.Codec.shape2_of_code}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Shape2, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.width_of_code, Turing.Cfg, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Suppose a bit string $y$ has the nested pairing form $\langle
x,\langle\operatorname{bits}(c),\langle\operatorname{bits}(c'),\operatorname{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$.
If a machine configuration on input $x$ has code $c$ at scale $s$, then $y$ has the
asserted two-payload shape: it has that nested pairing form, and the length of the
binary representation of $s$ is at most the length of the binary representation of $y$'s
length.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{7}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, the language
of pair-encoded tuples $(x,c,c',s)$ for which there are configurations on input $x$ with
work-tape heads and nonblank contents within radius $s$, whose configuration codes are
$c$ and $c'$, and where the second configuration follows from the first in one step of
$N$, is decidable in logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}
